text: Git is a popular version control system that helps developers manage changes to their code. One of its key features is branching, which allows you to create separate lines of development. A common practice is using feature branches, where you work on a new feature without affecting the main codebase. Once your work is complete, you can merge the branch back into the main branch. In team projects, developers often open a pull request before merging. This lets others review the code, discuss improvements, and catch mistakes. Following a clear version control workflow makes collaboration easier and keeps the project organized.
